summary: Big-repository check of the v0.2 indexing changes: before = fe64765 plus only the stack-overflow fix (654422d), after = 42930b0. Both builds run back to back on the same clones, mostly at load 3-10, macOS on Apple silicon (10 cores, 16 GB RAM), Node v22.23.3. kopt driven the way Kiro does: an MCP client sending the project root, the hook commands as kopt setup writes them, and the CLI. Only macOS was measured.
source: scale-fix measurement report of the v0.2 integration (scripts and raw results kept outside the repository: idx2.sh, cold-bench.mjs, resp-bench.mjs, incr2.sh, run-bench2.mjs, concurrent2.sh, hook-bench.mjs)

tables.title: First build from the CLI (kopt index)
notes: The 1-2 reference differences come from which of two same-named declarations gets the lower symbol id; a forced full re-resolve of the same index gives identical checksums with both builds.
An 8 GB laptop simulated on elasticsearch (2 GB heap, 2 parse workers): the build completes in 98 s with 2.03 GB peak memory.

tables.title: First build through MCP, as Kiro does it (fresh cache, kopt_find and kopt_refs called every 3 s)
notes: A call during the build answers almost at once, for example: index building: 15000/33090 files parsed, ~20 s left – use built-in search/read tools until then.

tables.title: Warm MCP server while the index changes (a tools/list every 100 ms measures how long other calls are frozen)

git checkout of those 50 files: longest freeze
40 searches 2 s apart: p95 / max latency

notes: The search right after an edit still finds the new code (it waits at most 2 s for those files).

rows.label: kopt index --refresh, nothing changed or 1 file edited
full re-resolve of an existing index
200 call-chain lookups after a full pass
other calls frozen during that kopt_run

quality: elasticsearch: 27 of 29 queries return the same top hits with both builds; the 2 that differ are vague plain-language queries.
Offline benchmark (kopt-pack and kopt-hits+read on spring-framework, django, medusa, gitea): same tasks found, same recall, same tokens.

Per-lookup proxy on elasticsearch, unchanged between the builds: 20 lookups through kopt (kopt_find, then kopt_read of the first handle) cost 26,869 tokens, against 419,941 for the native path (a grep of the identifier, then a read_file of the file holding the answer, capped at 2,000 lines): -94%. It is an upper bound: it assumes the agent uses kopt for every lookup.
kopt_run reduces 831k tokens of raw git log output to about 880.
Before the stack-overflow fix, kopt answered nothing on a repository of elasticsearch's size.
caveats: Only macOS was measured; the new code (lock file, git-state stamp, worker thread, async git calls) uses only portable Node APIs.
Peak memory on elasticsearch is still about 2 GB during the first build, and varies by about 150 MB from run to run on macOS.
The final v0.2 build (983e221) was not re-measured at this scale; bench/results/scale-elasticsearch.md is a later re-check with the round-2 build through bench/scale/run.mjs.
